title: Mirai Labs - Pilot acceptance criteria + security scoping
summary: POC scoping for a 3-week pilot to validate throughput, latency, and security controls. Main asks: SOC 2/ISO proof, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC granularity, audit logs and KMS integration. Agreed next steps: bench plan, share compliance pack, schedule SSO test, pilot ETA mid-July.
topics: success criteria definition (latency p95, throughput, error budget)
workload sizing and benchmark plan (concurrency, seq length)
security/compliance checklist: SOC 2, ISO 27001, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS/HSM
deployment modes: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-23
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/ff-20250623-mls-4872 (placeholder)
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Aiko (Mirai CTO), Marcus (Head of Platform), Priya (Security)

[00:00] Samira: Hi everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intros? We'll run through high level goals then get deep on security requirements and benching.
[00:08] Aiko: Hi, I'm Aiko, CTO at Mirai. We're evaluating Redwood to power an internal document QA assistant and a customer-facing summarization API.
[00:14] Marcus: Marcus, platform. We're responsible for infra, throughput, SLA.
[00:17] Priya: Priya, security. I'll be driving compliance and SSO integration.
[00:22] Samira: Great. Diego, do you want to frame the pilot?
[00:25] Diego: Sure. We're proposing a 3-week pilot — week 0 is setup and SSO, week 1 run benching, week 2 iterate and validate acceptance criteria. Pilot aims: p95 latency under 180ms for typical gen path at seq len ~512 tokens, sustain 120 concurrent sessions, and error rate under 1%. Also validate audit logs and KMS integration.
[00:45] Marcus: Quick clarifying q — 120 concurrent sessions, is that per-region or global?
[00:49] Diego: That's cluster-local for your EU region; we can split load. For hosted we'll probably route to nearest region.
[00:56] Priya: On security, we need SOC 2 Type II evidence, ISO 27001 certification if available, SSO via SAML (IdP is Okta), SCIM for provisioning, RBAC with at least three roles (admin/dev/observer), and immutable audit logs with retention controls. Also KMS/HSM for key material.
[01:12] Samira: Absolutely. We can share our SOC 2 report and ISO summary — Diego, confirm the KMS options?
[01:18] Diego: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations in Dedicated and Private. Hosted can support bring-your-own-key via our KMS connectors — there's a short onboarding though. HSM direct is available for Private installs. We'll note that our audit logs capture request metadata, tokenization events, and model selection; retention is configurable but default 90 days.
[01:36] Priya: Default 90 is probably too short for us — we need 1 year retention for audit logs, with options to export to an external SIEM (Splunk/Datadog). Can we stream logs to S3 or to our SIEM?
[01:46] Diego: Yes. We can configure streaming to S3 and syslog/HTTP endpoints. There's also an option to ship to a logging bucket in your VPC in Private deployments.
[01:54] Aiko: Data residency is important — some docs must stay in APAC. We want to run inference in an APAC region or on-prem. What's the effort for Private?
[02:03] Samira: Private is doable; typical timeline is 4–6 weeks to stand up in your environment, faster if you take our appliance. For a short pilot, Dedicated capacity in an APAC region might be fastest.
[02:15] Marcus: About success criteria: beyond latency and concurrency, we want throughput per GPU, token cost estimates, and regression checks on accuracy vs our baseline model. Also a sign-off step that security has no open findings.
[02:28] Diego: Agreed. Bench plan: we'll run two synthetic workloads — a short prompt low-latency stream (seq 256, beam/generation config X) and a long-context batch (seq 1024) to measure KV cache and memory behavior. We'll capture p50, p95, p99 latencies, cpu/gpu utilization, tokens/sec, and failure modes.
[02:45] Priya: For the audit trail we need mapping of who called the API, request IDs, model version, and redaction markers for PII. Do you provide built-in redaction or do we need to pre-process?
[02:55] Diego: We have optional prefix-layer redaction and can flag tokens via structured output or allow you to pre-scrub. Redaction accuracy is not perfect; recommend pre-filtering for PII in your initial pilot.
[03:07] Samira: Quick note on throttles — Redwood has route-level quotas and can do graceful fallback to a smaller model if capacity is constrained. Does that impact audit trace?
[03:14] Diego: It does add a switch in logs — we'll annotate fallback events.
[03:19] Marcus: On SSO, we want SAML SSO for the Console, and SAML for API token issuance via our IdP. Does Redwood support SP-initiated flow and SCIM for provisioning?
[03:29] Samira: Yes to SP-init and SCIM. There's a short setup guide; Diego will send a test plan.
[03:34] Priya: We also need RBAC per-model and per-team isolation. Can we ensure team A cannot call team B's models?
[03:40] Diego: Yes, we can create project-scoped API keys, and RBAC maps to projects. For Private/Dedicated you get network-level isolation too.
[03:47] Aiko: For the bench tests, what models will we use? We plan to compare Redwood-curated Llama-variant and an internal fine-tuned model.
[03:55] Diego: We'll test with a 13B Llama derived open checkpoint and provide a quantized variant if needed. For your internal model, we can host it during the pilot — we'll need the model artifacts and an ops window.
[04:05] Samira: Timeline recap: if we start setup next week, SSO and KMS onboarding in week 1, bench runs in week 2, analysis and acceptance in week 3 — target sign-off ~ mid-July.
[04:14] Marcus: Sounds reasonable. On acceptance gates, security sign-off is must-have; performance thresholds are soft fail/soft pass with follow-up tuning.
[04:22] Priya: For SOC 2, do you provide the mapping of controls to compliance evidence? We need to run our internal questionnaire.
[04:28] Samira: We'll share the SOC 2 cert and an evidence matrix mapping our controls to common customer requirements.
[04:34] Priya: Great. Also, do you support customer-managed encryption-in-transit certs (mTLS)?
[04:39] Diego: mTLS for Private and Dedicated yes; hosted can provide mutual TLS for private endpoints with some setup.
[04:46] Aiko: What about cost visibility during the pilot? Marcus wants token-level cost breakdown to estimate run-rate.
[04:52] Samira: The Console provides token/call dashboards and per-route cost estimation. Diego will pull sample billing CSVs.
[04:59] Marcus: Regarding benchmarks, please include end-to-end latency (client to token), not just inference. We want network + serialization overhead.
[05:06] Diego: We'll include network hops and instrument client SDKs.
[05:10] Priya: A small nit: retention/erasures. If a user requests data deletion, how is prompt/response data removed from logs and backups?
[05:18] Diego: We support on-demand deletions that scrub data from live logs and mark it for removal from backups. For forensic purpose we keep an audit stub (non-sensitive metadata). We'll document the deletion lifecycle.
[05:30] Samira: Ok let's capture action items and next steps.
[05:33] Aiko: Before we jump, any competitive comparisons to note?
[05:36] Diego: Customers often compare to managed endpoints from cloud vendors and to running a self-hosted runtime. Redwood differentiates on unified ops and out-of-the-box batching/caching.
[05:45] Priya: We did a quick look at vendor X (anonymized) — they lacked project-scoped keys and audit streaming.
[05:51] Samira: Thanks. We'll circle back with docs and the bench plan.
[05:55] Diego: I'll draft the bench test cases: concurrency sweep (20/60/120/240), seq len profiles, throughput vs cost, and failover scenarios.
[06:05] Marcus: We'll provide a workload sample dataset (sanitized) and traffic profile.
[06:10] Samira: Great. Next meeting? Suggest end of week after initial SSO setup to kick off the bench.
[06:16] Aiko: Friday 08:00 PDT works for us.
[06:19] Samira: Perfect — thanks all.

Note: Transcript has some automatic captions issues; product names occasionally mis-typed (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache).
